claim: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifts off from Cape Canaveral carrying Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL on NASA's NG-25 resupply mission to the International Space Station on Sunday 29 November 2026 (US Eastern Time).

runs.scenario: If liftoff occurs at 23:59:30 EST, one reader could count it because the wording 'through 23:59' includes that entire minute, while another could resolve NO because the explicit window ends at 23:59:00 EST.
runs.yes_requires: A SpaceX Falcon 9 carrying Cygnus NG-25 (NASA's Northrop Grumman CRS-25 mission) must lift off on November 29, 2026, within the stated EST window. A failure after liftoff still counts as YES.
runs.decided_by: NASA's ISS blog or a NASA news release, or an official SpaceX report, establishing the mission and its actual liftoff time.

runs.yes_requires: The SpaceX Falcon 9 carrying Northrop Grumman's Cygnus XL on NASA's NG-25 mission must lift off from Cape Canaveral between 00:00 and 23:59 EST on 29 November 2026 (including a liftoff followed by a launch failure).
runs.decided_by: NASA (ISS blog or news release) or SpaceX

runs.scenario: Liftoff is timestamped at 23:59:30 EST on 29 November 2026. One reader treats the criterion's '00:00 to 23:59' as including that whole minute (YES); the other applies the event window ending at 23:59:00 exactly (NO).
runs.yes_requires: A Falcon 9 carrying Cygnus NG-25 (NASA's Northrop Grumman CRS-25) lifts off between 00:00 and 23:59 EST on 29 November 2026 (America/New_York), as reported by NASA or SpaceX. Liftoff counts even if the launch later fails; a scrub, a delay outside that window, or an earlier launch is NO.
runs.decided_by: NASA (ISS blog or news release) or SpaceX
